name: LAPD calls for service
traps: Roughly 46% of records are officer-initiated (scene markers, traffic stops) rather than public calls — the raw total measures police deployment and RISES when patrols increase; split officer- from public-initiated or do not present it as neighborhood demand
notes: Fresher than the incident feed; useful when incident data lags

name: LAPD incident data, NIBRS era
traps: area_name is SPACE-PADDED to fixed width, so equality filters return 0 rows with HTTP 200 and look exactly like a quiet week — filter on the numeric district id and cross-check against an unfiltered group-by; the predecessor 2020-2024 dataset is frozen while its portal updatedAt still reads current
notes: City of LA only; superseded an earlier dataset at the NIBRS migration

name: City of Los Angeles open data
traps: WRONG JURISDICTION for the ~87 independent cities inside LA County, yet it outranks county sources in search; a ZIP filter can return a stray plausible row for an address outside city limits, so check row VOLUME rather than mere presence
notes: Use only when the ZIP is inside City of LA limits

name: LADBS building permits
traps: Runs about 7 days behind, so a nominal trailing week returns 0 permits — printed, that becomes a fabricated "none were issued"; measure the last complete window the data covers and name that window
notes: Has a real zip_code column, unusually easy to filter

name: LA County Assessor parcel roll
traps: Assessor parcel numbers (APN) resolve to a single property — treat as identifying, never print; the county portal is a different site from the City of LA portal
notes: Ownership and valuation roll covering every city in the county

name: LA County Sheriff incident data
traps: The Sheriff contracts policing for many independent cities — confirm whether your city has its own PD before using this; station and reporting-district geography does not align with ZIP boundaries
notes: Countywide incident records; the correct crime source for contract cities
